title: The Shallows Where Divergence Learns to Sound

features.name: the first fork
features.desc-on-touch: The water splits here and each branch sings. You can follow neither without losing the other, and something in that teaches you about divergence.

features.name: a stone that learned to listen
features.desc-on-touch: The stone sits mid-current. Where the water diverges around it, two separate echoes return, each convinced it is the only one.

features.name: the air above the parting
features.desc-on-touch: Mist rises where the branches separate. In the mist, two bird-calls, neither quite the same as the other. The divergence teaches itself how to sound.

inscription: where unified things learn their own names by singing them back in separate keys

file.name: Recordings_Divergent_BirdCalls_NSW_Estuary.mp3
file.note: Field recordings from one location, one hour apart, as breeding flocks depart—each species' call frequency shifts as distance grows, the estuary itself learning many conversations at once

reverie.title: REVERIE — dawn estuary, two listening to one sound become tw
narr: You stand thigh-deep and Katita listens upstream. The bird-call
between you splits into two frequencies—she hears the eastern register,
you hear the western decline. You turn to confirm. She is turning
to ask you the same question. The divergence is already happening.
The water receives both versions of what it was. Neither is wrong.

exits.label: back into the undertow's unified pull
where the separated voices rise toward the canopy
downstream to where divergence learns to reconcile
